translations.literal: Treatise 66
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 66

translations.literal: Guest Rites)
translations.idiomatic: Guest Rites)

sentences.zh: 籓國通禮山海諸國朝貢禮敕封籓服禮外國公使覲見禮

translations.literal: General Protocol for Vassal States; Tribute Protocol for Maritime Countries; Investiture Protocol for Tributary Domains; Protocol for Audiences with Foreign Envoys
translations.idiomatic: General Protocol for Vassal States; Tribute Protocol for Maritime Countries; Investiture Protocol for Tributary Domains; Protocol for Audiences with Foreign Envoys

sentences.zh: 內外王公相見禮京官相見禮直省官相見禮士庶相見禮

translations.literal: Protocol for Meetings among Inner and Outer Princes and Dukes; Protocol for Meetings among Capital Officials; Protocol for Meetings among Provincial Officials; Protocol for Meetings among Scholars and Commoners
translations.idiomatic: Protocol for Meetings among Inner and Outer Princes and Dukes; Protocol for Meetings among Capital Officials; Protocol for Meetings among Provincial Officials; Protocol for Meetings among Scholars and Commoners

sentences.zh: 四曰賓禮。

translations.literal: The fourth [category] is Guest Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth category of rites is Guest Rites.

sentences.zh: 清初籓服有二類，分隸理籓院、主客司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing, tributary domains fell into two categories, subordinate respectively to the Court of Colonial Affairs and the Host and Guest Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qing dynasty, tributary domains fell into two categories, respectively subordinate to the Court of Colonial Affairs and the Host and Guest Bureau.

sentences.zh: 隸院者，蒙古喀爾喀，西藏、青海、廓爾喀是也；

translations.literal: Those subordinate to the Court were the Khalkha Mongols, Tibet, Qinghai, and Gorkha;
translations.idiomatic: Those under the Court were the Khalkha Mongols, Tibet, Qinghai, and Gorkha;

sentences.zh: 隸司者，曰朝鮮，曰越南，曰南掌，曰緬甸，曰蘇祿，曰荷蘭，曰暹羅，曰琉球。

translations.literal: Those subordinate to the Bureau were Korea, Vietnam, Lan Xang, Burma, Sulu, Holland, Siam, and Ryukyu.
translations.idiomatic: Those under the Bureau were Korea, Vietnam, Lan Xang, Burma, Sulu, Holland, Siam, and Ryukyu.

sentences.zh: 親疏略判，於禮同為屬也。

translations.literal: Though closeness and distance were broadly distinguished, in ritual terms they were all alike tributary.
translations.idiomatic: Though degrees of closeness and distance were broadly distinguished, in ritual terms they were all alike tributary domains.

sentences.zh: 西洋諸國，始亦屬於籓部，逮咸、同以降，歐風亞雨，咄咄逼人，覲聘往來，締結齊等，而於禮則又為敵。

translations.literal: The Western nations were at first also counted among the vassal departments; from the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns onward, as European influence pressed upon Asia, audiences and embassies were exchanged and treaties concluded on equal terms, and in ritual they came to be treated as equals.
translations.idiomatic: The Western nations were at first also counted among the vassal departments; from the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns onward, as European influence pressed upon Asia, audiences and embassies were exchanged and treaties were concluded on equal terms, and in ritual they came to be treated as equals rather than as vassals.

sentences.zh: 夫詩歌「有客」，傳載「交鄰」，無論屬國、與國，要之，來者皆賓也。

translations.literal: Whether in the Odes' "There Are Guests," or in the traditions concerning "Relations with Neighbors"—whether vassal states or coequal states, in the end all who come are guests.
translations.idiomatic: Whether in the Odes' "There Are Guests," or in the traditions concerning "Relations with Neighbors"—whether vassal states or coequal states, in the end all who come are guests.

sentences.zh: 我為主人，凡所以將事，皆賓禮也。

translations.literal: We are the hosts; all measures taken to receive them belong to Guest Rites.
translations.idiomatic: We are the hosts; all measures taken to receive them belong to Guest Rites.

sentences.zh: 茲編分著其儀節，而王公百官相見禮與士庶相見禮，亦附識焉。

translations.literal: This compilation sets forth their ceremonies in detail; the protocols governing meetings among princes and officials, and among scholars and commoners, are also appended.
translations.idiomatic: This compilation sets forth their ceremonies in detail; the protocols governing meetings among princes and officials, and among scholars and commoners, are also appended.

sentences.zh: 籓國通禮清初，蒙古北部喀爾喀三汗同時納貢。

translations.literal: General Protocol for Vassal States: At the beginning of the Qing, the three Khalkha khans of northern Mongolia simultaneously submitted tribute.
translations.idiomatic: General Protocol for Vassal States: At the beginning of the Qing, the three Khalkha khans of northern Mongolia simultaneously submitted tribute.

sentences.zh: 朔漠蕩平，懷柔漸遠。

translations.literal: The northern deserts were pacified, and conciliation extended ever farther.
translations.idiomatic: The northern deserts were pacified, and imperial conciliation extended ever farther.

sentences.zh: 北逾瀚海，西絕羌荒。

translations.literal: To the north it crossed the Gobi; to the west it reached beyond the Qiang frontier.
translations.idiomatic: To the north the realm crossed the Gobi; to the west it reached beyond the Qiang frontier.

sentences.zh: 青海厄魯特，西藏準噶爾，悉隸版圖。

translations.literal: The Oirats of Qinghai and the Dzungars of Tibet all came under the imperial domain.
translations.idiomatic: The Oirats of Qinghai and the Dzungars of Tibet all came under the imperial domain.

sentences.zh: 荷蘭亦受朝敕稱王，名列籓服。

translations.literal: Holland also received an imperial patent of investiture as king and was listed among the tributary domains.
translations.idiomatic: Holland also received an imperial patent of investiture as king and was listed among the tributary domains.

sentences.zh: 厥後至者彌眾，乃令各守疆圉、修職貢，設理籓院統之。

translations.literal: Afterward those who came grew ever more numerous; they were ordered each to guard their borders and fulfill tribute duties, and the Court of Colonial Affairs was established to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward those who came grew ever more numerous; they were ordered each to guard their borders and fulfill tribute duties, and the Court of Colonial Affairs was established to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 崇德間，定制，外籓諸部貝勒等有大勛績，封和碩親王，或多羅郡王，次多羅貝勒，遣使持信約往封。

translations.literal: During the Chongde reign regulations were fixed: banner princes of the outer vassal departments who had great merit were enfeoffed as prince of the first rank, or prince of the second rank, or banner lord of the third rank, and envoys were dispatched bearing credentials to invest them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongde reign regulations were fixed: banner princes of the outer vassal departments who had great merit were enfeoffed as prince of the first rank, prince of the second rank, or banner lord of the third rank, and envoys were dispatched bearing credentials to invest them.

sentences.zh: 既入境，貝勒出迎五里外，跽俟制冊過，騎以從。

translations.literal: Once the envoy entered their territory, the banner prince went out to welcome him five li beyond the border, knelt and waited until the patent passed, then mounted and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the envoy entered their territory, the banner prince went out to welcome him five li beyond the border, knelt and waited until the patent passed, then mounted and followed.

sentences.zh: 抵府，設香案正中，使臣奉冊其上，退立左旁，貝勒一叩三跪。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the princely residence, an incense table was set in the center; the envoy placed the patent upon it and withdrew to stand at the left; the banner prince performed one kowtow and three kneelings.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the princely residence, an incense table was set in the center; the envoy placed the patent upon it and withdrew to stand at the left; the banner prince performed one kowtow and three kneelings.

sentences.zh: 畢，興，復跪，使臣授冊。

translations.literal: When this was finished, he rose, knelt again, and the envoy handed him the patent.
translations.idiomatic: When this was finished, he rose, knelt again, and the envoy handed him the patent.

sentences.zh: 宣讀官宣畢，置原案，三叩，興。

translations.literal: After the court reader finished reading the investiture decree, the patent was replaced on the table; he kowtowed three times and rose.
translations.idiomatic: After the court reader finished reading the investiture decree, the patent was replaced on the table; he kowtowed three times and rose.

sentences.zh: 受冊如初禮。

translations.literal: Receiving the patent followed the initial ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the patent followed the initial ceremony.

sentences.zh: 貝勒與使臣對行六叩禮。

translations.literal: The banner prince and the envoy exchanged six kowtows facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: The banner prince and the envoy exchanged six kowtows facing each other.

sentences.zh: 使臣坐左，貝勒坐右。

translations.literal: The envoy sat on the left; the banner prince sat on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy sat on the left; the banner prince sat on the right.

sentences.zh: 事訖，躬送如前。

translations.literal: When the business was concluded, he escorted the envoy out in person as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the business was concluded, he escorted the envoy out in person as before.

sentences.zh: 凡有詔敕、賞賚至亦如之。

translations.literal: Whenever imperial edicts or gifts arrived, the same procedure was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever imperial edicts or gifts arrived, the same procedure was followed.

sentences.zh: 內外札薩克會盟，三年一舉。

translations.literal: Inner and outer jasak princes convened in league every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer jasak princes convened in league every three years.

sentences.zh: 使臣齎制往，迎送禮同。

translations.literal: Envoys bearing imperial patents went to them; the reception and send-off ceremonies were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys bearing imperial patents went to them; the reception and send-off ceremonies were the same.

sentences.zh: 自王以降，歲時朝貢者，分年番代，列班末行禮。

translations.literal: From princes downward, those who came annually on tribute were rotated by year-class, and performed rites at the end of the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: From princes downward, those who came annually on tribute were rotated by year-class, and performed rites at the end of the court ranks.

sentences.zh: 坐次視內親王、貝勒、貝子、公降一等，宴賚有差。

translations.literal: Seating was one grade below inner princes, banner lords, banner sons, and dukes; banquets and gifts varied by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Seating was one grade below inner princes, banner lords, banner sons, and dukes; banquets and gifts varied by rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十九年，定朝覲年例。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year of Kangxi, the annual schedule for court audiences was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year of Kangxi, the annual schedule for court audiences was fixed.

sentences.zh: 蒙古二十四部為兩班，喀爾喀札薩克等為四班。

translations.literal: The twenty-four Mongol banners formed two rotations; the Khalkha jasaks and others formed four rotations.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-four Mongol banners formed two rotations; the Khalkha jasaks and others formed four rotations.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，帝念四十九旗王公台吉遠至勤勞，詔改三班，二歲一朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, the emperor, mindful of the long journey and labor of the princes and taiji of the forty-nine banners, decreed a change to three rotations, with audiences every two years.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, the emperor, mindful of the long journey and labor of the princes and taiji of the forty-nine banners, decreed a change to three rotations, with audiences every two years.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，以蒙古汗王等遠道輸將，諭令停止年班。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, because the Mongol khans and princes made the long journey to bring tribute, an edict ordered the annual rotation to cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, because the Mongol khans and princes made the long journey to bring tribute, an edict ordered the annual rotation to cease.

sentences.zh: 御前行走者，番上如故。

translations.literal: Those who served at the imperial presence continued to rotate on duty as before.
translations.idiomatic: Those who served at the imperial presence continued to rotate on duty as before.

sentences.zh: 其貢獻儀文，按季各旗遣一人來將事，年時貢馬匹羊酒，交理籓院轉納禮部。

translations.literal: As for the ceremonial form of tribute, each banner sent one person each season to handle the business; each year they presented horses, sheep, and wine, which were submitted through the Court of Colonial Affairs to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: As for the ceremonial form of tribute, each banner sent one person each season to handle the business; each year they presented horses, sheep, and wine, which were submitted through the Court of Colonial Affairs to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 朝貢賞賚諸典，柔遠清吏司掌之。

translations.literal: The regulations governing tribute and rewards were administered by the Softening the Distant Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations governing tribute and rewards were administered by the Softening the Distant Bureau.

sentences.zh: 山海諸國朝貢禮凡諸國以時修貢，遣陪臣來朝，延納燕賜，典之禮部。

translations.literal: Tribute Protocol for Maritime Countries: Whenever the various states paid tribute on schedule and dispatched attendant ministers to court, their reception and banquet gifts were regulated by the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute Protocol for Maritime Countries: Whenever the various states paid tribute on schedule and dispatched attendant ministers to court, their reception and banquet gifts were regulated by the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 將入境，所在長吏給郵符，遴文武官數人伴送。

translations.literal: When they were about to enter the border, the local chief official issued travel passes and selected several civil and military officials to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to enter the border, the local chief official issued travel passes and selected several civil and military officials to escort them.

sentences.zh: 有司供館餼，遣兵護之。

translations.literal: The responsible officials supplied lodging and provisions and dispatched soldiers to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials supplied lodging and provisions and dispatched soldiers to guard them.

sentences.zh: 按途更代，以達京畿。

translations.literal: Escorts were replaced along the route until they reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Escorts were replaced along the route until they reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 既至，延入賓館，以時稽其人眾，均其飲食。

translations.literal: Once they arrived, they were received into the guest house; their numbers were checked in due course and their food and drink apportioned.
translations.idiomatic: Once they arrived, they were received into the guest house; their numbers were checked in due course and their food and drink apportioned.

sentences.zh: 翼日，具表文、方物，暨從官各服其服，詣部俟階下。

translations.literal: The next day they prepared the memorial, local products, and each attendant dressed in his own nation's garb, and went to the ministry to wait below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they prepared the memorial, local products, and each attendant dressed in his own nation's garb, and went to the ministry to wait below the steps.

sentences.zh: 儀制司官設表案堂中，質明，會同四譯館卿率貢使至禮部，侍郎一人出立案左，儀制司官二人分立左右楹。

translations.literal: An official of the Ceremonial Regulations Bureau set out the memorial table in the hall; at dawn the director of the Four Translators Institutes led the tribute envoys to the Ministry of Rites; one vice minister came out and stood to the left of the table; two Ceremonial Regulations officials stood one at each hall pillar.
translations.idiomatic: An official of the Ceremonial Regulations Bureau set out the memorial table in the hall; at dawn the director of the Four Translators Institutes led the tribute envoys to the Ministry of Rites; one vice minister came out and stood to the left of the table; two Ceremonial Regulations officials stood one at each hall pillar.

sentences.zh: 館卿先升，立左楹西。

translations.literal: The institute director ascended first and stood west of the left pillar.
translations.idiomatic: The institute director ascended first and stood west of the left pillar.

sentences.zh: 通事、序班各二人，引貢使等升階跪。

translations.literal: Two interpreters and two ushers each guided the tribute envoys up the steps to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Two interpreters and two ushers each guided the tribute envoys up the steps to kneel.

sentences.zh: 正使舉表，館卿祗受，以授侍郎，陳案上，復位。

translations.literal: The chief envoy raised the memorial; the institute director received it reverently and handed it to the vice minister, who placed it on the table; then he returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The chief envoy raised the memorial; the institute director received it reverently and handed it to the vice minister, who placed it on the table; then he returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 使臣等行三跪九叩禮，興。

translations.literal: The envoys performed three kneelings and nine kowtows, then rose.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys performed three kneelings and nine kowtows, then rose.

sentences.zh: 退，館卿率之出。

translations.literal: They withdrew, and the institute director led them out.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew, and the institute director led them out.

sentences.zh: 禮部官送表內閣俟命，貢物納所司。

translations.literal: Ministry officials sent the memorial to the Grand Secretariat to await orders; the tribute goods were delivered to the appropriate department.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials sent the memorial to the Grand Secretariat to await orders; the tribute goods were delivered to the appropriate department.

sentences.zh: 如值大朝常朝，序班引貢使等列西班末，聽贊行禮如儀。

translations.literal: If it fell on a grand audience or regular audience day, ushers led the tribute envoys to stand at the end of the west rank, and on the herald's cue they performed the rites according to protocol.
translations.idiomatic: If it fell on a grand audience or regular audience day, ushers led the tribute envoys to stand at the end of the west rank, and on the herald's cue they performed the rites according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 非朝期則禮部先奏，若召見，館卿豫戒習儀。

translations.literal: On non-audience days the Ministry of Rites submitted a memorial first; if an audience was granted, the institute director instructed them beforehand in court etiquette.
translations.idiomatic: On non-audience days the Ministry of Rites submitted a memorial first; if an audience was granted, the institute director instructed them beforehand in court etiquette.

sentences.zh: 屆日帝御殿，禮部尚書引貢使入，通事隨行，至丹墀西行禮畢，升自西階，通事復從之。

translations.literal: On the appointed day the emperor held court; the minister of rites led the tribute envoys in, with interpreters following; they performed rites in the western courtyard, then ascended by the west steps, and the interpreters followed again.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the emperor held court; the minister of rites led the tribute envoys in, with interpreters following; they performed rites in the western courtyard, then ascended by the west steps, and the interpreters followed again.

sentences.zh: 及殿門外跪，帝慰問，尚書承傳，通事轉諭，貢使對辭，通事譯言，尚書代奏。

translations.literal: They knelt outside the hall gates; the emperor inquired after them; the minister received and relayed his words; the interpreter translated them; the envoys replied; the interpreter rendered their words; and the minister reported on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: They knelt outside the hall gates; the emperor inquired after them; the minister received and relayed his words; the interpreter translated them; the envoys replied; the interpreter rendered their words; and the minister reported on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 畢，乃退。

translations.literal: When this was finished, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When this was finished, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 如示優異，則丹墀行禮畢，即引入殿右門，立右翼大臣末，通事立少後。

translations.literal: If special favor was shown, after the courtyard rites were finished they were led in through the right hall door, standing after the right-wing ministers, with the interpreter standing slightly behind.
translations.idiomatic: If special favor was shown, after the courtyard rites were finished they were led in through the right hall door, standing after the right-wing ministers, with the interpreter standing slightly behind.

sentences.zh: 賜坐、賜茶，均隨大臣跪叩，飲畢，慰問傳答如初。

translations.literal: When seated reception and tea were granted, they knelt and kowtowed along with the ministers; after drinking, inquiries and replies proceeded as before.
translations.idiomatic: When seated reception and tea were granted, they knelt and kowtowed along with the ministers; after drinking, inquiries and replies proceeded as before.

sentences.zh: 出朝所，賜尚方飲食，退。

translations.literal: Leaving the audience hall, they were granted food from the imperial kitchen, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the audience hall, they were granted food from the imperial kitchen, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 翼日赴午門外謝恩。

translations.literal: The next day they went outside the Meridian Gate to express thanks for the imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they went outside the Meridian Gate to express thanks for the imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 禮部疏請頒賜國王並燕賚貢使，既得旨，所司陳賜物午門道左，館卿率貢使等東面立，侍郎西面立，有司咸序。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites submitted a memorial requesting permission to distribute gifts to the king and banquet the tribute envoys; once the order was received, the responsible officials arranged the gifts to the east of the Meridian Gate road; the institute director led the tribute envoys to stand facing east, the vice minister stood facing west, and all officials took their places in order.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites submitted a memorial requesting permission to distribute gifts to the king and banquet the tribute envoys; once the order was received, the responsible officials arranged the gifts to the east of the Meridian Gate road; the institute director led the tribute envoys to stand facing east, the vice minister stood facing west, and all officials took their places in order.

sentences.zh: 貢使詣西墀三跪九叩，主客司官頒賜物授貢使，貢使跪受。

translations.literal: The tribute envoys approached the west platform and performed three kneelings and nine kowtows; an official of the Host Bureau bestowed the gifts and handed them to the envoys, who received them kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: The tribute envoys approached the west platform and performed three kneelings and nine kowtows; an official of the Host Bureau bestowed the gifts and handed them to the envoys, who received them kneeling.

sentences.zh: 以次頒賜貢使暨從官從人，咸跪受。

translations.literal: Gifts were then distributed in order to the tribute envoys, their attendants, and their servants; all received them kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts were then distributed in order to the tribute envoys, their attendants, and their servants; all received them kneeling.

sentences.zh: 贊「興，叩」如儀。

translations.literal: On the herald's call of "Rise and kowtow," they did so according to protocol.
translations.idiomatic: On the herald's call of "Rise and kowtow," they did so according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 退，賜宴禮部。

translations.literal: They withdrew, and a banquet was granted at the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew, and a banquet was granted at the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 貢使將歸國，光祿寺備牲酒果蔬，侍郎就賓館筵燕，伴送供偫如前。

translations.literal: When the tribute envoys were about to return home, the Court of Imperial Entertainments prepared meat, wine, and fruit; the vice minister feasted them at the guest house; escort and provisions were supplied as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribute envoys were about to return home, the Court of Imperial Entertainments prepared meat, wine, and fruit; the vice minister feasted them at the guest house; escort and provisions were supplied as before.

sentences.zh: 所經省會皆饗之，司道一人主其事，館餼日給，概從周渥焉。

translations.literal: Every provincial capital along the route entertained them; one circuit intendant supervised the matter; lodging and provisions were supplied daily—all generously provided.
translations.idiomatic: Every provincial capital along the route entertained them; one circuit intendant supervised the matter; lodging and provisions were supplied daily—all generously provided.

sentences.zh: 順治初，定制，諸國朝貢，齎表及方物，限船三艘，艘百人，貢役二十人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi regulations were fixed: for tribute missions from the various states, bearing memorials and local products, the limit was three ships, one hundred men per ship, and twenty tribute bearers.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shunzhi regulations were fixed: for tribute missions from the various states, bearing memorials and local products, the limit was three ships, one hundred men per ship, and twenty tribute bearers.

sentences.zh: 十三年，俄國察罕汗遣使入貢，以不諳朝儀，卻其貢，遣之歸。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Tsar of Russia sent envoys to present tribute; because they were unfamiliar with court ritual, their tribute was refused and they were sent home.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, the Tsar of Russia sent envoys to present tribute; because they were unfamiliar with court ritual, their tribute was refused and they were sent home.

sentences.zh: 明年復表貢，途經三載，表文仍不合體制。

translations.literal: The next year they again presented a memorial tribute; the journey took three years, and the memorial still did not conform to required form.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they again presented a memorial tribute; the journey took three years, and the memorial still did not conform to required form.

sentences.zh: 世祖以外邦從化，宜予涵容，量加恩賞，諭令毋入覲。

translations.literal: The Shunzhi Emperor, deeming the foreign state had submitted in good faith, granted generous rewards and ordered that they need not seek audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunzhi Emperor, deeming the foreign state had submitted in good faith, granted generous rewards and ordered that they need not seek audience.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十二年，俄復遣使義茲柏阿朗迭義迭來朝，帝始召見，賜坐賜食。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi, Russia again sent the envoy Nicolis Spafari to court; the emperor received him in audience for the first time and granted seated reception and food.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi, Russia again sent the envoy Nicolis Spafari to court; the emperor received him in audience for the first time and granted seated reception and food.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，葡萄牙使臣斐拉理入覲，帝御九經三事殿。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, the Portuguese envoy Frairi was received in audience; the emperor held court in the Hall of the Nine Classics and Three Matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year, the Portuguese envoy Frairi was received in audience; the emperor held court in the Hall of the Nine Classics and Three Matters.

sentences.zh: 使者入殿左門，升左陛，進表御座則膝行。

translations.literal: The envoy entered through the left hall door, ascended the left steps, and advanced to the imperial throne on his knees.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy entered through the left hall door, ascended the left steps, and advanced to the imperial throne on his knees.

sentences.zh: 帝受表，使者興，出，凡出入皆三跪九叩。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial; the envoy rose and withdrew; on every entry and exit he performed three kneelings and nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the memorial; the envoy rose and withdrew; on every entry and exit he performed three kneelings and nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 賜坐賜茶，謝恩如儀。

translations.literal: Seated reception and tea were granted; thanks for the imperial grace followed protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Seated reception and tea were granted; thanks for the imperial grace followed protocol.

sentences.zh: 初，琉球、安南、暹羅諸使來，議政大臣咸會集，賜坐及茶。

translations.literal: At first, when envoys from Ryukyu, Annam, and Siam came, the grand secretaries all assembled and were granted seated reception and tea.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when envoys from Ryukyu, Annam, and Siam came, the grand secretaries all assembled and were granted seated reception and tea.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初元，諭停止。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign, an edict ordered this discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign, an edict ordered this discontinued.

sentences.zh: 時屬國陪臣增擴，敕所司給皇清職貢圖，以詔方來。

translations.literal: At that time, as tributary attendants expanded in number, officials were ordered to distribute the Imperial Tribute Atlas to instruct those who would come.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, as tributary attendants expanded in number, officials were ordered to distribute the Imperial Tribute Atlas to instruct those who would come.

sentences.zh: 四十七年正月，紫光閣錫燕，朝鮮、琉球、南掌陪臣與焉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-seventh year, a feast was granted at the Ziguang Pavilion; attendant ministers from Korea, Ryukyu, and Lan Xang were among those present.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the forty-seventh year, a feast was granted at the Ziguang Pavilion; attendant ministers from Korea, Ryukyu, and Lan Xang were among those present.

sentences.zh: 燕罷，賜珍物。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, precious gifts were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended, precious gifts were granted.

sentences.zh: 五十年，舉千叟宴，特命朝鮮賀正陪臣齒逾六十者充正、副使，預宴賦詩。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, at the banquet of a thousand elders, Korean New Year envoys over sixty were specially appointed chief and deputy envoys to attend the feast and compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year, at the banquet of a thousand elders, Korean New Year envoys over sixty were specially appointed chief and deputy envoys to attend the feast and compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 越五年，安南國王阮光平來京祝壽，定行禮班序，列親王、郡王間，其陪臣仍附班末。

translations.literal: Five years later, the king of Annam, Nguyen Quang Binh, came to the capital to congratulate the emperor on his birthday; his ceremonial rank was fixed between princes of the first and second rank, while his attendants still stood at the end of the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later, the king of Annam, Nguyen Quang Binh, came to the capital to congratulate the emperor on his birthday; his ceremonial rank was fixed between princes of the first and second rank, while his attendants still stood at the end of the ranks.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，英吉利入貢，使臣瑪戛爾等覲見，自陳不習拜跪，及至御前，而跽伏自若。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, England presented tribute; the envoys Macartney and others were received in audience; they declared themselves unaccustomed to kneeling and kowtowing, yet when they came before the throne they prostrated themselves quite naturally.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year, England presented tribute; the envoys Macartney and others were received in audience; they declared themselves unaccustomed to kneeling and kowtowing, yet when they came before the throne they prostrated themselves quite naturally.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初元，再舉千叟宴，朝鮮、安南、暹羅、廓爾喀額爾德尼王吉爾巴納足塔畢噶爾瑪薩九叩，「跪奉大皇帝前：竊小臣聞湖南教匪滋事，致天威震怒，遣兵剿除。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiaqing reign, the banquet of a thousand elders was held again; Korea, Annam, Siam, and the king of Gorkha, Girbanazutabigarmasa, performed nine kowtows, kneeling to address the Great Emperor: "Your humble subject heard that bandits in Hunan provoked the imperial wrath and troops were dispatched to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiaqing reign, the banquet of a thousand elders was held again; Korea, Annam, Siam, and the king of Gorkha, Girbanazutabigarmasa, performed nine kowtows, kneeling to address the Great Emperor: "Your humble subject heard that bandits in Hunan provoked the imperial wrath and troops were dispatched to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 今已平定，聞之忻慰。

translations.literal: Now that order has been restored, I am heartened to hear it.
translations.idiomatic: Now that order has been restored, I am heartened to hear it.

sentences.zh: 小臣受恩深重，虔修土產微物，表文，叩賀天喜。

translations.literal: Your humble subject, deeply indebted for imperial grace, reverently offers local products and a memorial to congratulate Heaven's joy.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble subject, deeply indebted for imperial grace, reverently offers local products and a memorial to congratulate Heaven's joy.

sentences.zh: 小臣屬蒙天恩，視如子民，唯有一心歸順，和睦鄰封。

translations.literal: Your humble subject, granted Heaven's favor and regarded as your own people, has but one wish—to remain loyal and live in harmony with neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble subject, granted Heaven's favor and regarded as your own people, has but one wish—to remain loyal and live in harmony with neighboring states.

sentences.zh: 小臣陽布離京遠，年尚幼，伏墾當作奴輩，曲施教導，霑恩不淺」云云。

translations.literal: Your humble subject Yangbu, though far from the capital and still young, humbly entreats that when I serve as attendant (the text's Fu Ken should read attendants), you will kindly instruct me, for the grace would not be slight," and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble subject Yangbu, though far from the capital and still young, humbly entreats that when I serve among the attendants, you will kindly instruct me, for the grace would not be slight," and so forth.

sentences.zh: 其貢物計十二事，語質意恭如此。

translations.literal: Their tribute comprised twelve items; the language was plain and the intent respectful in this manner.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute comprised twelve items; the language was plain and the intent respectful in this manner.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，英復遣使來貢，執事者告以須行拜跪禮，司當冬等遂稱疾不入覲，帝怒，諭遣歸國，罷筵宴賜物。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, England again sent envoys to present tribute; the officials told them they must perform the kneeling and kowtowing rites; Lord Amherst and others then claimed illness and refused audience; the emperor in anger ordered them sent home and canceled the banquet and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, England again sent envoys to present tribute; the officials told them they must perform the kneeling and kowtowing rites; Lord Amherst and others then claimed illness and refused audience; the emperor in anger ordered them sent home and canceled the banquet and gifts.

sentences.zh: 嗣是英使不復來庭。

translations.literal: Thereafter English envoys no longer came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter English envoys no longer came to court.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，回疆敉定，上太后徽號，緬甸國王遣使進金葉表，創舉也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang, after the Muslim frontier was pacified and honorific titles were conferred upon the empress dowager, the king of Burma sent envoys presenting a memorial on gold leaf—a first.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daoguang, after the Muslim frontier was pacified and honorific titles were conferred upon the empress dowager, the king of Burma sent envoys presenting a memorial on gold leaf—a first.

sentences.zh: 故事，琉球間歲一貢，至十九年，詔改四年為期。

translations.literal: By precedent, Ryukyu paid tribute every other year; in the nineteenth year an edict changed the interval to four years.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, Ryukyu paid tribute every other year; in the nineteenth year an edict changed the interval to four years.

sentences.zh: 時國王尚育咨達閩撫吳文鎔，謂琉球瀕海，地患多風，朝貢以時，風雨和順，歲則大熟。

translations.literal: At that time King Shō Iku consulted the Fujian governor Wu Wenrong, saying that Ryukyu faced the sea and suffered frequent winds; when tribute came on schedule, wind and rain were harmonious and the year brought a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: At that time King Shō Iku consulted the Fujian governor Wu Wenrong, saying that Ryukyu faced the sea and suffered frequent winds; when tribute came on schedule, wind and rain were harmonious and the year brought a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 貢舶出入閩疆，歲頒時憲書，獲以因時趨事。

translations.literal: Tribute ships entering and leaving Fujian received the calendar each year, enabling them to time their affairs to the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute ships entering and leaving Fujian received the calendar each year, enabling them to time their affairs to the seasons.

sentences.zh: 地不產藥，賴舶載回應用。

translations.literal: The land produced no medicines; they relied on returning ships to bring back what was needed.
translations.idiomatic: The land produced no medicines; they relied on returning ships to bring back what was needed.

sentences.zh: 至航海針法，非隨時練習不為功。

translations.literal: As for nautical compass technique, unless practiced constantly it cannot be mastered.
translations.idiomatic: As for nautical compass work, it cannot be mastered without constant practice at sea.

sentences.zh: 若改四年，則恐豐歉不齊，人時莫授，藥品既缺，針盤益疏，請復舊制便。

translations.literal: If changed to four years, there is fear that harvests would be uneven, men and seasons would not align, medicines would be lacking, and compass skills would grow rusty; please restore the old system for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: If the interval were changed to four years, harvests might be uneven, men and seasons would fall out of step, medicines would run short, and compass skills would grow rusty; he asked that the old biennial system be restored.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The report was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 並令陪臣子弟得隨貢使入監讀書。

translations.literal: Attendants' sons were also ordered permitted to enter the Directorate of Education with tribute envoys to study.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants' sons were also permitted to enter the Imperial Academy with tribute envoys to study.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十四年，廓爾喀入貢，賞正使噶箕二品服，副使四品服，其將事時，服色即各從其品，亦前此所未有者。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Guangxu, Gorkha presented tribute; the chief envoy was granted robes of the second rank, the deputy envoy robes of the fourth rank; when performing their duties, the colors of their robes matched their respective ranks—something without precedent until then.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year of Guangxu, Gorkha presented tribute; the chief envoy was granted robes of the second rank and the deputy envoy robes of the fourth rank; when performing their duties, the colors of their robes matched their respective ranks—something without precedent until then.

sentences.zh: 凡貢期，朝鮮歲至，琉球間歲一至，安南六歲再至，暹羅三歲，荷蘭、蘇祿五歲，南掌十歲，均各一至，餘道遠貢無常期。

translations.literal: As for tribute schedules: Korea came annually; Ryukyu once every other year; Annam once every six years; Siam every three years; Holland and Sulu every five years; Lan Xang every ten years—each once per interval; the rest, being distant, had no fixed schedule.
translations.idiomatic: As for tribute schedules: Korea came annually; Ryukyu once every other year; Annam once every six years; Siam every three years; Holland and Sulu every five years; Lan Xang every ten years—each once per interval; the more distant states had no fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 凡貢物，各將其土實，非土產者勿進。

translations.literal: As for tribute goods, each state was to present its genuine local products; items not native to the soil were not to be offered.
translations.idiomatic: As for tribute goods, each state was to present its genuine local products; items not native to the land were not to be offered.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮、安南、琉球、緬甸、蘇祿、南掌皆有常物，餘唯其所獻。

translations.literal: Korea, Annam, Ryukyu, Burma, Sulu, and Lan Xang all had fixed tribute items; the rest presented whatever they chose.
translations.idiomatic: Korea, Annam, Ryukyu, Burma, Sulu, and Lan Xang all had fixed tribute items; the rest presented whatever they chose.

sentences.zh: 敕封籓服禮清自太宗征服朝鮮，鑱石三田渡。

translations.literal: Investiture Protocol for Tributary Domains: From the Qing Taizong's conquest of Korea, a stone was inscribed at Sandian Ferry.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture Protocol for Tributary Domains: From the Qing Taizong's conquest of Korea, a commemorative stone was carved at Sandian Ferry.

sentences.zh: 厥後安南、琉球諸國，先後請封，皆遣使往。

translations.literal: Afterward Annam, Ryukyu, and other states successively requested investiture, and envoys were dispatched to each.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Annam, Ryukyu, and other states successively requested investiture, and envoys were dispatched to each in turn.

sentences.zh: 其他回首內鄉者，航海匪夐，梯山忘阻，則璽書褒獎，授來使齎還而已。

translations.literal: Other tribes who turned inward to submit, though the sea route was long and mountain paths arduous, received only imperial letters of praise to be carried back by their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Other tribes who turned inward to submit, though distant by sea and arduous by mountain paths, received only imperial letters of praise to be carried back by their envoys.

sentences.zh: 崇德間，定制，凡外邦效順，俱頒冊錫爵。

translations.literal: During the Chongde reign regulations were fixed: all foreign states that submitted received patents and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongde reign regulations were fixed: all foreign states that submitted in good faith received patents of investiture and ranks of nobility.

sentences.zh: 進奏書牘，署大清紀年。

translations.literal: Memorials and documents submitted bore the era name of the Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials and official documents submitted bore the era name of the Great Qing.

sentences.zh: 若朝貢諸國無子嗣位，則遣陪臣請朝命，禮部奏遣正、副使各一人持節往封，特賜一品麒麟服以重其行。

translations.literal: If a tributary state had no heir to succeed, attendant ministers were sent to request imperial orders; the Ministry of Rites memorialized to dispatch one chief and one deputy envoy bearing credentials to invest the successor, specially granting first-rank qilin robes to honor their mission.
translations.idiomatic: If a tributary state had no heir to succeed to the throne, attendant ministers were sent to request imperial orders; the Ministry of Rites memorialized to dispatch one chief and one deputy envoy bearing credentials to invest the successor, specially granting first-rank qilin robes to honor their mission.

sentences.zh: 行日，工部給旗仗，兵部給乘傳。

translations.literal: On the day of departure, the Ministry of Works provided banners and insignia, and the Ministry of War provided post horses.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of departure, the Ministry of Works provided banners and insignia, and the Ministry of War provided post horses.

sentences.zh: 封使詣禮部，儀制司官一人奉節，一人奉詔敕，授本部長官，以授正、副使，跪受。

translations.literal: The investiture envoys went to the Ministry of Rites; one Ceremonial Regulations official bore the credentials, another bore the edict; they were handed to the ministry chief, who passed them to the chief and deputy envoys, who received them kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: The investiture envoys went to the Ministry of Rites; one Ceremonial Regulations official bore the credentials and another bore the edict; these were handed to the ministry chief, who passed them to the chief and deputy envoys, who received them kneeling.

sentences.zh: 興，出易征衣乘傳往。

translations.literal: They rose, went out, changed into travel dress, and departed by post horse.
translations.idiomatic: They rose, went out, changed into travel dress, and departed by post horse.

sentences.zh: 將入境，其國邊吏備館傳夫馬。

translations.literal: When they were about to enter the border, that state's frontier officials prepared lodges, relay stations, porters, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to enter the border, that state's frontier officials prepared guest lodges, relay stations, porters, and horses.

sentences.zh: 緣途所經，有司跪接。

translations.literal: Along the route, local officials knelt to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route, local officials knelt to receive them.

sentences.zh: 及國，嗣封王遣陪臣郊迎，三跪九叩，勞使者一跪三叩。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the state, the heir to be invested sent attendant ministers to welcome them at the suburbs; they performed three kneelings and nine kowtows, and to honor the envoys performed one kneeling and three kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the state, the heir to be invested sent attendant ministers to welcome them in the suburbs; they performed three kneelings and nine kowtows, and to honor the envoys performed one kneeling and three kowtows.

sentences.zh: 延入館，陳詔節龍亭內，行禮如儀。

translations.literal: They were received into the guest house; the edict, credentials, and dragon pavilion were set up inside, and rites were performed according to protocol.
translations.idiomatic: They were received into the guest house; the edict, credentials, and dragon pavilion were set up inside, and rites were performed according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 謁使者三叩，不答。

translations.literal: The heir paid respects to the envoys with three kowtows; they did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The heir paid respects to the envoys with three kowtows; they did not respond in kind.

sentences.zh: 諏日，王率陪臣詣館，禮畢，王先歸。

translations.literal: A date was chosen; the king led attendant ministers to the guest house; when the rites were finished, the king returned first.
translations.idiomatic: A date was chosen; the king led attendant ministers to the guest house; when the rites were finished, the king returned first.

sentences.zh: 龍亭舁行，仗樂前導，封使後隨。

translations.literal: The dragon pavilion was carried in procession, ceremonial guards and music leading the way, the investiture envoys following behind.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon pavilion was carried in procession, with ceremonial guards and music leading the way and the investiture envoys following behind.

sentences.zh: 入門陳正中，使者及階下馬，正使奉節，副使奉詔敕，入殿陳案上，退立東旁。

translations.literal: Upon entering the gate it was placed in the center; the envoys dismounted at the steps; the chief envoy bore the credentials, the deputy envoy bore the edict and patent; they entered the hall and placed them on the table, then withdrew to stand east of it.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering the gate it was placed in the center; the envoys dismounted at the steps; the chief envoy bore the credentials and the deputy envoy bore the edict and patent; they entered the hall, placed them on the table, and withdrew to stand to the east.

sentences.zh: 王率眾官北面立，三跪九叩，興，詣封位前跪。

translations.literal: The king led all officials to stand facing north; they performed three kneelings and nine kowtows, rose, and proceeded to kneel before the investiture seat.
translations.idiomatic: The king led all officials to stand facing north; they performed three kneelings and nine kowtows, rose, and proceeded to kneel before the investiture seat.

sentences.zh: 副使奉詔書付宣讀官，宣訖，王行禮如初，出俟門外。

translations.literal: The deputy envoy handed the investiture edict to the reading officer; when the reading was finished, the king performed the rites as before, then withdrew to wait outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy envoy handed the investiture edict to the reading officer; when the reading was finished, the king performed the rites as before, then withdrew to wait outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 使者出，跪送。

translations.literal: The envoys came out; the king knelt to send them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys came out, the king knelt to send them off.

sentences.zh: 有間，適館勞之。

translations.literal: After an interval, he went to the guest house to host them.
translations.idiomatic: After an interval, he went to the guest house to entertain them.

sentences.zh: 使者還朝，乃修表文，具方物，遣陪臣詣闕謝恩。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned to court, the king then drafted a memorial, prepared local products, and dispatched attendant ministers to the palace to express thanks for the imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys returned to court, the king drafted a memorial, prepared local products, and dispatched attendant ministers to the palace to express thanks for the imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 如諭祭兼冊封，先於其祖廟將事，諭祭文陳案上，使者左右立。

translations.literal: If an edict ordered sacrificial rites together with investiture, the ceremony was first performed at the ancestral temple; the sacrificial edict was placed on a table, with the envoys standing to either side.
translations.idiomatic: If an edict ordered sacrificial rites together with investiture, the ceremony was first performed at the ancestral temple; the sacrificial edict was placed on a table, with the envoys standing to either side.

sentences.zh: 世子跪叩如前，退立神位左，乃宣讀，眾俯伏。

translations.literal: The heir apparent kneeled and kowtowed as before, withdrew to stand at the left of the spirit tablet, then the edict was read aloud and all prostrated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent kneeled and kowtowed as before, withdrew to stand at the left of the spirit tablet, then the edict was read aloud and all prostrated themselves.

sentences.zh: 宣畢，興。

translations.literal: When the reading was finished, they rose.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished, they rose.

sentences.zh: 送燎行禮，使者退。

translations.literal: The sacrificial offerings were sent to be burned and rites performed; the envoys withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial offerings were sent to be burned and the rites performed; the envoys withdrew.

sentences.zh: 次行冊封禮，儀與前同。

translations.literal: Next the investiture ceremony was performed, with the same protocol as before.
translations.idiomatic: Next the investiture ceremony was performed, following the same protocol as before.

sentences.zh: 至以詔敕授使齎還，則禮部設案午門，位正中，尚書立案左。

translations.literal: When an edict and patent were to be entrusted to envoys to carry back, the Ministry of Rites set a table at the Meridian Gate, positioned in the center, with the minister standing to the left of the table.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict and patent were to be entrusted to envoys to carry back, the Ministry of Rites set a table at the Meridian Gate in the center, with the minister standing to the left of the table.

sentences.zh: 儀制司官從館卿率來使入，授詔敕，序班引詣案前跪，授受如制。

translations.literal: A Ceremonial Regulations official, together with the institute director, led the incoming envoys in; the edict and patent were handed over; ushers guided them to kneel before the table, and presentation and reception followed the prescribed form.
translations.idiomatic: A Ceremonial Regulations official, together with the institute director, led the incoming envoys in; the edict and patent were handed over; ushers guided them to kneel before the table, and presentation and reception followed the prescribed form.

sentences.zh: 退詣丹墀西，三跪九叩，禮成，歸授國王。

translations.literal: They withdrew to the west of the red courtyard, performed three kneelings and nine kowtows, and when the rites were complete, returned to present them to their king.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew to the west of the red courtyard, performed three kneelings and nine kowtows, and when the rites were complete, returned to present them to their king.

sentences.zh: 謝恩同。

translations.literal: Thanks for the imperial grace followed the same procedure.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks for the imperial grace followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 外國公使覲見禮康熙初，外洋始入貢，中朝款接，稍異籓服。

translations.literal: Protocol for Audiences with Foreign Envoys: At the beginning of Kangxi, Western countries first began sending tribute; the central court received them with a manner slightly different from that for tributary domains.
translations.idiomatic: Protocol for Audiences with Foreign Envoys: At the beginning of Kangxi, Western countries first began sending tribute; the central court received them in a manner slightly different from that for tributary domains.

sentences.zh: 南懷仁官欽天監，贈工部侍郎，凡內廷召見，並許侍立，不行拜跪禮。

translations.literal: Ferdinand Verbiest held office in the Directorate of Astronomy and was posthumously granted the rank of vice minister of works; whenever summoned to the inner court, he was permitted to stand in attendance and was not required to perform kneeling or kowtowing rites.
translations.idiomatic: Ferdinand Verbiest held office in the Directorate of Astronomy and was posthumously granted the rank of vice minister of works; whenever summoned to the inner court, he was permitted to stand in attendance and was not required to kneel or kowtow.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，羅馬教皇遣使來京，世宗許行西禮，且與握手。

translations.literal: During Yongzheng, the Pope of Rome sent envoys to the capital; the Yongzheng Emperor permitted them to use Western etiquette and even shook hands with them.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongzheng, the Pope of Rome sent envoys to the capital; the Yongzheng Emperor permitted them to use Western etiquette and even shook hands with them.

sentences.zh: 乾隆季葉，英使馬格里入覲，禮臣與議儀式，彼以覲見英王為言，特旨允用西禮。

translations.literal: In the late Qianlong period, the English envoy Markham was received in audience; ritual officials discussed the ceremony with him; citing the manner of audience before the King of England, a special edict permitted the use of Western etiquette.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Qianlong period, the English envoy Markham was received in audience; ritual officials discussed the ceremony with him; citing the manner of audience before the King of England, a special edict permitted the use of Western etiquette.

sentences.zh: 筵宴日，且親賜卮酒。

translations.literal: On the banquet day, the emperor personally bestowed a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: On the banquet day, the emperor personally bestowed a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 商約既締，將命頻繁。

translations.literal: Once commercial treaties were concluded, diplomatic missions became frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Once commercial treaties were concluded, diplomatic missions became frequent.

sentences.zh: 咸、同間，外國使臣嘗求入覲，時以禮制乖異，力拒之。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns, foreign envoys repeatedly sought audiences, but at the time, because ritual forms differed, they were firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns, foreign envoys repeatedly sought audiences, but because ritual forms differed, they were firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 同治時，英、法使臣固請再四，我猶繩以華制，莫之應。

translations.literal: During Tongzhi, British and French envoys repeatedly pressed their requests, yet we still held them to Chinese protocol and did not accede.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongzhi, British and French envoys repeatedly pressed their requests, yet the court still held them to Chinese protocol and did not accede.

sentences.zh: 彼且曰，宜亟修好，阻其入覲，是靳以客禮也。

translations.literal: They said in reply that good relations ought to be promptly restored, and that barring them from audience was to stint them of guest courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: They said in reply that good relations ought to be promptly restored, and that barring them from audience was to stint them of the courtesy due to guests.

sentences.zh: 十二年，穆宗親政，泰西使臣環請瞻覲，呈國書，先自言用西禮，折腰者三，廷臣力言其不便。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Muzong Emperor personally assumed rule; Western envoys all petitioned for audiences and presented their credentials, stating beforehand that they would use Western etiquette—bowing at the waist three times; court ministers strongly argued that this would be unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the Muzong Emperor personally assumed rule; Western envoys all petitioned for audiences and presented their credentials, stating beforehand that they would use Western etiquette—bowing at the waist three times; court ministers strongly argued that this would be unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 直隸總督李鴻章建議，略言：「先朝召見西使時，各國未立和約，各使未駐京師，國勢雖強，不逮今日，猶得律以升殿受表常儀。

translations.literal: The Governor-General of Zhili, Li Hongzhang, submitted a memorial suggesting, in summary: "When the previous reign summoned Western envoys to audience, the various states had not yet concluded treaties, their envoys were not yet resident in the capital, and though their national strength was great, it did not match today; yet they could still be governed by the regular court ritual of ascending the hall to present memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The Governor-General of Zhili, Li Hongzhang, submitted a memorial suggesting, in summary: "When the previous reign summoned Western envoys to audience, the various states had not yet concluded treaties, their envoys were not yet resident in the capital, and though their national strength was great, it did not match today; yet they could still be governed by the regular court ritual of ascending the hall to present memorials.

sentences.zh: 然嘉慶中，英使來朝，已不行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: Yet in the Jiaqing reign, when English envoys came to court, they already did not perform the three kneelings and nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Jiaqing reign, when English envoys came to court, they already did not perform the three kneelings and nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 厥後成約，儼然均敵，未便以屬禮相繩。

translations.literal: Thereafter treaties were concluded and they stood as equals; it is no longer fitting to bind them with vassal rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter treaties were concluded and they stood as equals; it was no longer fitting to bind them with vassal rites.

sentences.zh: 拒而不見，似於情未洽。

translations.literal: To refuse audience seems insufficiently warm in sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: To refuse audience seemed insufficiently warm in sentiment.

sentences.zh: 糾以跪拜，又似所見不廣。

translations.literal: To insist on kneeling and kowtowing seems unduly narrow in outlook.
translations.idiomatic: To insist on kneeling and kowtowing seemed unduly narrow in outlook.

sentences.zh: 第取其敬有餘，當恕其禮不足。

translations.literal: Only take that their respect exceeds requirements, and forgive where their etiquette falls short.
translations.idiomatic: Only take that their respect exceeded requirements, and forgive where their etiquette fell short.

sentences.zh: 惟宜議立規條，俾相遵守。

translations.literal: It is only fitting to establish regulations for mutual observance.
translations.idiomatic: It was only fitting to establish regulations for mutual observance.

sentences.zh: 各使之來，許一見，毋再見，許一時同見，毋單班求見，當可杜其覬覦。

translations.literal: When envoys come, permit one audience but not a second; permit them to be received together at one time but not to seek individual audiences—thus their covetous hopes may be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys came, permit one audience but not a second; permit them to be received together at one time but not to seek individual audiences—thus their covetous hopes could be cut off.

sentences.zh: 且禮與時變通，我朝待屬國有定制，待與國無定禮。

translations.literal: Moreover, ritual adapts with the times; our dynasty has fixed forms for tributary states but no fixed ritual for coequal states.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, ritual adapts with the times; our dynasty had fixed forms for tributary states but no fixed ritual for coequal states.

sentences.zh: 近今商約，實數千年變局，國家無此禮例，往聖亦未豫定禮經，是在酌時勢權宜以樹之准。」

translations.literal: The recent commercial treaties represent a transformation unseen in thousands of years; the state has no precedent for such ritual, and the sages of old did not prescribe it in the ritual classics—the task is to weigh the times and circumstances and establish a provisional standard."
translations.idiomatic: The recent commercial treaties represented a transformation unseen in thousands of years; the state had no precedent for such ritual, and the sages of old did not prescribe it in the ritual classics—the task was to weigh the times and circumstances and establish a provisional standard."

sentences.zh: 時總理各國事務恭親王以拜跪儀節往復申辨，而各使堅執如初。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Gong, who supervised affairs with foreign countries, repeatedly debated the kneeling and kowtowing protocol back and forth, but the various envoys held firm to their original position.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Gong, who supervised affairs with foreign countries, repeatedly debated the kneeling and kowtowing protocol back and forth, but the various envoys held firm to their original position.

sentences.zh: 勢難終拂其意，乃為奏請，明諭允行。

translations.literal: Finding it difficult to ultimately go against their wishes, he submitted a memorial requesting explicit imperial approval to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Finding it difficult to ultimately go against their wishes, he submitted a memorial requesting explicit imperial approval, which was granted.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，日本使臣副島種臣、俄使臣倭良嘎哩、美使臣鏤斐迪、英使臣威妥瑪、法使臣熱福理、和蘭使臣費果蓀瞻覲紫光閣，呈國書，依商訂例行事。

translations.literal: That summer, the Japanese envoy Soejima Taneomi, the Russian envoy Yariga, the American envoy Frederick Low, the English envoy Thomas Wade, the French envoy Revell, and the Dutch envoy Vigoonsen were received in audience at the Ziguang Pavilion, presented their credentials, and followed the agreed commercial protocol.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, the Japanese envoy Soejima Taneomi, the Russian envoy Yariga, the American envoy Frederick Low, the English envoy Thomas Wade, the French envoy Revell, and the Dutch envoy Vigoonsen were received in audience at the Ziguang Pavilion, presented their credentials, and followed the agreed commercial protocol.

sentences.zh: 接見時，帝坐立唯意，賜茗酒，恩自上出。

translations.literal: During the reception, the emperor might sit or stand as he pleased, and tea and wine were granted as imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: During the reception, the emperor might sit or stand as he pleased; tea and wine were granted as imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 使臣訊安否，謹致賀辭。

translations.literal: The envoys inquired after his health and respectfully offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys inquired after his health and respectfully offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 未垂問，毋先言事。

translations.literal: Without imperial inquiry, they were not to broach official business first.
translations.idiomatic: Without imperial inquiry, they were not to broach official business first.

sentences.zh: 西例臣見君鞠躬三，今改五鞠躬。

translations.literal: By Western custom a subject bowed three times before his sovereign; this was changed to five bows.
translations.idiomatic: By Western custom a subject bowed three times before his sovereign; this was changed to five bows.

sentences.zh: 使臣初至始覲見，餘則否。

translations.literal: Envoys received audience only upon first arrival; thereafter they did not.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys received audience only upon first arrival; thereafter they did not.

sentences.zh: 嗣後親奉國書者仿此。

translations.literal: Henceforth those who personally bore credentials were to follow this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth those who personally bore credentials were to follow this precedent.

sentences.zh: 其禮式先期繪圖試習，覲見某處所，某月日時，並候旨行。

translations.literal: The ritual forms were diagrammed and rehearsed in advance; the place, date, and hour of audience were all determined by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual forms were diagrammed and rehearsed in advance; the place, date, and hour of audience were all determined by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 其大略也。

translations.literal: Such were the general outlines.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the general outlines.

sentences.zh: 光緒十六年，駐英使臣薛福成奏陳：「各使覲見，須定明例。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Guangxu, the envoy stationed in England, Xue Fucheng, submitted a memorial stating: "Audiences for the various envoys must be established by clear precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Guangxu, the envoy stationed in England, Xue Fucheng, submitted a memorial stating: "Audiences for the various envoys must be established by clear precedent.

sentences.zh: 凡使臣初至一國，其君莫不延見慰勞，使臣謁畢，鞠躬退，語不及公。

translations.literal: Whenever an envoy first arrives in a country, its sovereign invariably extends an audience and words of comfort; after the envoy pays his respects and bows and withdraws, private conversation does not touch public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an envoy first arrives in a country, its sovereign invariably extends an audience and words of comfort; after the envoy pays his respects, bows, and withdraws, private conversation does not touch public affairs.

sentences.zh: 此通例也。

translations.literal: This is the universal practice.
translations.idiomatic: This is the universal practice.

sentences.zh: 頃聞駐京公使，以未蒙晝接，不無私議。

translations.literal: It has lately been heard that the envoys resident in the capital, because they have not been granted a daytime audience, harbor private dissatisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: It had lately been heard that the envoys resident in the capital, because they had not been granted a daytime audience, harbored private dissatisfaction.

sentences.zh: 昔年英使威妥瑪藉詞不令入覲，致煙台條款多要挾，靳虛文而受實損，非計之得。

translations.literal: In years past the English envoy Thomas Wade used the pretext of being denied audience to drive hard bargains in the Chefoo Convention, grasping at empty formalities while suffering real losses—this was not a wise policy.
translations.idiomatic: In years past the English envoy Thomas Wade used the pretext of being denied audience to drive hard bargains in the Chefoo Convention, grasping at empty formalities while suffering real losses—this was not a wise policy.

sentences.zh: 今宜循同治十二年成案，援據以行。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to follow the precedent established in the twelfth year of Tongzhi and apply it accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Now it was fitting to follow the precedent established in the twelfth year of Tongzhi and apply it accordingly.

sentences.zh: 若論禮節，可於召見先敕下所司，中禮西禮，假以便宜。

translations.literal: As for etiquette, an edict may be issued in advance of the summons to the responsible officials, blending Chinese and Western forms and granting discretionary latitude.
translations.idiomatic: As for etiquette, an edict could be issued in advance of the summons to the responsible officials, blending Chinese and Western forms and granting discretionary latitude.

sentences.zh: 如是，彼雖行西禮，仍於體制無損。」

translations.literal: Thus, though they perform Western rites, the institutional framework remains undiminished."
translations.idiomatic: Thus, though they performed Western rites, the institutional framework would remain undiminished."

sentences.zh: 云云。

translations.literal: — and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: — and so forth.

sentences.zh: 自是遂為定例。

translations.literal: From this it became fixed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: From this it became fixed precedent.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，聯軍平拳匪，各國挾求更改禮節。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the allied armies suppressed the Boxer rebels, and the various powers demanded changes to ceremonial protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, the allied armies suppressed the Boxer rebels, and the various powers demanded changes to ceremonial protocol.

sentences.zh: 謂各使臣會同覲見，必在太和殿。

translations.literal: They insisted that joint audiences of all envoys must take place in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: They insisted that joint audiences of all envoys must take place in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 一國使臣單行覲見者，必在乾清宮。

translations.literal: Audiences for a single envoy from one country must take place in the Palace of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: Audiences for a single envoy from one country must take place in the Palace of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 呈遞國書，必遣乘輿往迓，至宮殿前降輿，禮成送歸。

translations.literal: When presenting credentials, an imperial sedan must be dispatched to meet them; they dismounted before the palace hall, and after the rites were complete they were escorted back.
translations.idiomatic: When presenting credentials, an imperial sedan must be dispatched to meet them; they were to dismount before the palace hall, and after the rites were complete they were to be escorted back.

sentences.zh: 齎奏國書，必自中門入，帝必躬親接受。

translations.literal: When bearing memorials and credentials, they must enter through the central gate, and the emperor must personally receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When bearing memorials and credentials, they must enter through the central gate, and the emperor must personally receive them.

sentences.zh: 設宴乾清宮，帝必躬親入座。

translations.literal: Banquets were to be held in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, and the emperor must personally take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Banquets were to be held in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, and the emperor must personally take his seat.

sentences.zh: 嗣復允會同覲見改在乾清宮，而轎用黃色。

translations.literal: Later it was also agreed that joint audiences would be moved to the Palace of Heavenly Purity, while the sedans used would be yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was also agreed that joint audiences would be moved to the Palace of Heavenly Purity and that yellow sedans would be used.

sentences.zh: 於是慶親王奕劻等以天澤堂廉之辨，不能每事曲從。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince Qing and others, mindful of the distinction between imperial majesty and the dignity of the hall, could not accede to every demand.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Prince Qing and others, mindful of the distinction between imperial majesty and the dignity of the hall, could not accede to every demand.

sentences.zh: 遂與各使磋商，歷時數月，始將乘坐黃轎、太和殿覲見暨宮殿階前降輿三事酌議改易，而爭議始息。

translations.literal: They then negotiated with the various envoys; after several months, agreement was finally reached to modify the three points concerning yellow sedans, audiences in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and dismounting before the palace steps—and only then did the disputes cease.
translations.idiomatic: They then negotiated with the various envoys; after several months, agreement was finally reached to modify the three points concerning yellow sedans, audiences in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and dismounting before the palace steps—and only then did the disputes cease.

sentences.zh: 各國親王覲見儀，始光緒二十四年。

translations.literal: The protocol for audiences with foreign princes began in the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu.
translations.idiomatic: The protocol for audiences with foreign princes began in the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu.

sentences.zh: 德國親王亨利入覲，帝幸頤和園，御仁壽殿，亨利公服入，遞國書，帝慰勞之。

translations.literal: The German Prince Henry was received in audience; the emperor went to the Summer Palace and held court in the Hall of Benevolent Longevity; Prince Henry entered in formal dress, presented his credentials, and the emperor comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The German Prince Henry was received in audience; the emperor went to the Summer Palace and held court in the Hall of Benevolent Longevity; Prince Henry entered in formal dress, presented his credentials, and the emperor comforted him.

sentences.zh: 既，亨利慾覲皇太后，帝奉懿旨代見。

translations.literal: Afterward Prince Henry wished to pay respects to the empress dowager; the emperor received him on her behalf by her express command.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Prince Henry wished to pay respects to the empress dowager; the emperor received him on her behalf by her express command.

sentences.zh: 是日巳刻，御玉瀾堂，亨利偕德使海靖等入，外部司官引殿東便門外入布幄少憩。

translations.literal: That day at the si hour, the emperor held court at the Hall of Jade Ripples; Prince Henry entered together with the German envoy Heinrich von Heiden and others; officials of the foreign ministry led them in through the east side gate of the hall to rest briefly in the canvas tent.
translations.idiomatic: That day at the si hour, the emperor held court at the Hall of Jade Ripples; Prince Henry entered together with the German envoy Heinrich von Heiden and others; officials of the foreign ministry led them in through the east side gate of the hall to rest briefly in the canvas tent.

sentences.zh: 駕至，扈從如儀，鳴鞭三，升座。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession arrived, the escort formed as prescribed; the whip was cracked three times, and the emperor ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession arrived, the escort formed as prescribed; the whip was cracked three times, and the emperor ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 慶親王等侍左右，外部長官率亨利等自中門入，北鄉一鞠躬，行數武又一鞠躬，至龍柱前又一鞠躬。

translations.literal: Prince Qing and others attended at his sides; the chief of the foreign ministry led Prince Henry and the others in through the central gate; facing north, they bowed once, after several paces bowed again, and upon reaching the dragon pillars bowed once more.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qing and others attended at his sides; the chief of the foreign ministry led Prince Henry and the others in through the central gate; facing north, they bowed once, after several paces bowed again, and upon reaching the dragon pillars bowed once more.

sentences.zh: 然後奉國書進，慶親王降左階接受，陳玉案，亨利等又一鞠躬，帝頷首答之，操國語慰勞。

translations.literal: They then advanced to present their credentials; Prince Qing descended the left steps to receive them and placed them on the jade table; Prince Henry and the others bowed again, and the emperor nodded in reply and offered words of comfort in the national language.
translations.idiomatic: They then advanced to present their credentials; Prince Qing descended the left steps to receive them and placed them on the jade table; Prince Henry and the others bowed again, and the emperor nodded in reply and offered words of comfort in the national language.

sentences.zh: 慶親王跪案左聆玉音，降階，操漢語傳宣。

translations.literal: Prince Qing knelt at the left of the table to listen to the jade voice, then descended the steps and relayed the message in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qing knelt at the left of the table to listen to the imperial words, then descended the steps and relayed the message in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 德繙譯官譯畢，亨利等又一鞠躬，帝仍頷首答之。

translations.literal: When the German interpreter had finished translating, Prince Henry and the others bowed again, and the emperor again nodded in reply.
translations.idiomatic: When the German interpreter had finished translating, Prince Henry and the others bowed again, and the emperor again nodded in reply.

sentences.zh: 亨利等退數武又一鞠躬，退至堂左，又一鞠躬。

translations.literal: Prince Henry and the others withdrew several paces and bowed again, then withdrew to the left of the hall and bowed once more.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Henry and the others withdrew several paces and bowed again, then withdrew to the left of the hall and bowed once more.

sentences.zh: 禮成。

translations.literal: The rites were complete.
translations.idiomatic: The rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 內外王公相見禮崇德初元，定宗室外籓親王、郡王、貝勒、貝子相見儀。

translations.literal: Protocol for Meetings among Inner and Outer Princes and Dukes. In the first year of Chongde, the protocol for meetings among imperial-clan and outer-vassal princes of the first rank, princes of the second rank, banner lords, and banner sons was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Protocol for Meetings among Inner and Outer Princes and Dukes. In the first year of the Chongde reign, regulations were set for how imperial-clan and outer-vassal princes of the first rank, princes of the second rank, banner lords, and banner sons were to meet one another.

sentences.zh: 賓及門，王府屬官入告，主人降階迎，賓辭，主人升。

translations.literal: When the guest reached the gate, an official of the princely household entered to announce him; the host descended the steps to welcome him; the guest declined; the host ascended.
translations.idiomatic: When the guest arrived at the gate, a household official went in to announce him. The host came down the steps to welcome him; the guest demurred, and the host returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 賓從自中門入，賓趨左，主人趨右。

translations.literal: The guest's attendants entered through the central gate; the guest hastened to the left, the host to the right.
translations.idiomatic: The guest's attendants entered through the central gate. The guest moved quickly to the left and the host to the right.

sentences.zh: 行相見禮，二跪六叩，即席序立。

translations.literal: They performed the meeting rite of two kneelings and six kowtows, then took their places at the seats in order and stood.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged the meeting salutation—two kneelings and six kowtows—then took their assigned places at the seats and stood.

sentences.zh: 從官升東階，行禮亦如之。

translations.literal: The attending officials ascended the eastern steps and performed the rite likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The attending officials mounted the eastern steps and performed the same rite.

sentences.zh: 興，入右門，坐賓後。

translations.literal: They arose, entered through the right gate, and sat behind the guest.
translations.idiomatic: They rose, passed through the right gate, and seated themselves behind the guest.

sentences.zh: 執事獻茶，賓受茶，叩，主人答叩。

translations.literal: The attendants presented tea; the guest received the tea, kowtowed, and the host returned the kowtow.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought tea. The guest accepted it, kowtowed, and the host returned the kowtow.

sentences.zh: 飲茶敘語畢，從官趨前楹，跪，叩，興，趨出。

translations.literal: After tea and conversation were finished, the attending officials hastened to the front eaves, knelt, kowtowed, arose, and hastened out.
translations.idiomatic: When tea and conversation were finished, the attending officials hurried to the front eaves, knelt and kowtowed, rose, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賓離席跪叩，主人答叩，並興。

translations.literal: The guest left his seat, knelt, and kowtowed; the host returned the kowtow; both arose.
translations.idiomatic: The guest rose from his seat, knelt, and kowtowed; the host returned the kowtow, and both stood up.

sentences.zh: 賓出，主人降階送，屬官送門外。

translations.literal: The guest departed; the host descended the steps to see him off, and the household officials escorted him outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The guest left. The host came down the steps to see him off, and household officials escorted him beyond the gate.

sentences.zh: 若外籓郡王見，則主人迎送殿外，不降階。

translations.literal: If an outer-vassal prince of the second rank came to call, the host welcomed and saw him off outside the hall without descending the steps.
translations.idiomatic: When an outer-vassal prince of the second rank paid a visit, the host welcomed and saw him off outside the hall but did not come down the steps.

sentences.zh: 相見，賓二跪六叩，主人答半。

translations.literal: At the meeting, the guest performed two kneelings and six kowtows, and the host returned half.
translations.idiomatic: At the meeting the guest performed two kneelings and six kowtows, and the host returned half of them.

sentences.zh: 賓辭退，跪叩，主人答跪不叩。

translations.literal: When the guest took leave, he knelt and kowtowed; the host returned by kneeling but did not kowtow.
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave the guest knelt and kowtowed; the host responded by kneeling but did not kowtow in return.

sentences.zh: 餘如親王儀。

translations.literal: The remainder followed the protocol for princes of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed the protocol for princes of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 外籓貝勒見，主人離坐迎，不出殿，賓北面跪叩如初，主人立受。

translations.literal: When an outer-vassal banner lord called, the host rose from his seat to welcome him without leaving the hall; the guest faced north, knelt, and kowtowed as before; the host received standing.
translations.idiomatic: When an outer-vassal banner lord came to call, the host rose from his seat to welcome him but did not leave the hall. The guest faced north, knelt, and kowtowed as before, and the host received the salutation standing.

sentences.zh: 即席正坐，賓侍坐。

translations.literal: They took their seats properly; the guest sat in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: They took their proper seats, with the guest sitting in attendance.

sentences.zh: 辭退跪叩，主人立受不送。
