translations.literal: On taking leave the guest knelt and kowtowed; the host received standing and did not see him off.
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave the guest knelt and kowtowed; the host received the salutation standing and did not escort him out.

sentences.zh: 餘如郡王儀。

translations.literal: The remainder followed the protocol for princes of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed the protocol for princes of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 外籓貝子、公見，府屬官引賓入殿，跪叩同。

translations.literal: When an outer-vassal banner son or duke called, a household official led the guest into the hall; kneeling and kowtowing were the same.
translations.idiomatic: When an outer-vassal banner son or duke came to call, a household official led the guest into the hall, and the kneeling and kowtowing were the same.

sentences.zh: 辭退仍跪叩，主人皆坐受。

translations.literal: On taking leave they still knelt and kowtowed; the host received all while seated.
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave they still knelt and kowtowed, and the host received the salutation seated throughout.

sentences.zh: 餘如貝勒儀。

translations.literal: The remainder followed the banner-lord protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed the banner-lord protocol.

sentences.zh: 外籓親王見郡王，主人迎送大門內，餘與親王相見同。

translations.literal: When an outer-vassal prince of the first rank called on a prince of the second rank, the host welcomed and saw him off inside the great gate; the remainder was the same as when princes of the first rank met.
translations.idiomatic: When an outer-vassal prince of the first rank called on a prince of the second rank, the host welcomed and saw him off inside the great gate; the rest followed the protocol for meetings between princes of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 郡王見郡王亦如之。

translations.literal: When a prince of the second rank called on another prince of the second rank, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When one prince of the second rank called on another, the same rules applied.

sentences.zh: 其外籓貝勒見郡王，如郡王見親王禮。

translations.literal: When an outer-vassal banner lord called on a prince of the second rank, it followed the protocol for a prince of the second rank calling on a prince of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: When an outer-vassal banner lord called on a prince of the second rank, the protocol was the same as when a prince of the second rank called on a prince of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 以下賓主相見，降殺遞差。

translations.literal: Below this, guest and host meetings declined in grade by successive steps.
translations.idiomatic: For meetings below this level, the honors due guest and host were reduced in graduated steps according to rank.

sentences.zh: 外籓親王見貝勒，主人迎送門外。

translations.literal: When an outer-vassal prince of the first rank called on a banner lord, the host welcomed and saw him off outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When an outer-vassal prince of the first rank called on a banner lord, the host welcomed and saw him off outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 賓入，主人從，相見各一跪三叩。

translations.literal: The guest entered; the host followed; at the meeting each performed one kneeling and three kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The guest entered and the host followed. At the meeting each performed one kneeling and three kowtows.

sentences.zh: 外籓郡王暨貝勒見貝勒同。

translations.literal: When an outer-vassal prince of the second rank or a banner lord called on a banner lord, it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: When an outer-vassal prince of the second rank or another banner lord called on a banner lord, the protocol was the same.

sentences.zh: 外籓貝子、公見貝勒，賓一跪三叩，主人跪拱手受。

translations.literal: When an outer-vassal banner son or duke called on a banner lord, the guest performed one kneeling and three kowtows; the host knelt, clasped his hands, and received.
translations.idiomatic: When an outer-vassal banner son or duke called on a banner lord, the guest performed one kneeling and three kowtows, and the host knelt, clasped his hands, and received the salutation.

sentences.zh: 外籓王、貝勒見貝子，賓主一跪一叩坐，此其異者也。

translations.literal: When an outer-vassal prince or banner lord called on a banner son, guest and host performed one kneeling and one kowtow and then sat—this was what differed.
translations.idiomatic: When an outer-vassal prince or banner lord called on a banner son, guest and host performed one kneeling and one kowtow and then sat down—this was the distinctive feature.

sentences.zh: 京官相見禮順治元年，定制，京朝官敵體相見，賓及門，主人迎大門內，揖賓入，及階，讓升，賓西主東。

translations.literal: Protocol for Meetings among Capital Officials. In the first year of Shunzhi regulations were fixed: when capital officials of equal rank met, when the guest reached the gate the host welcomed him inside the great gate, bowed with hands joined to admit the guest, and at the steps each yielded precedence to ascend—the guest on the west, the host on the east.
translations.idiomatic: Protocol for Meetings among Capital Officials. In the first year of Shunzhi, regulations were fixed for capital officials of equal standing to meet one another. When the guest arrived at the gate, the host welcomed him inside the great gate and bowed with joined hands to admit him. At the steps each yielded precedence to the other to ascend—the guest on the west, the host on the east.

sentences.zh: 及廳事，讓入，皆北面再拜。

translations.literal: When they reached the reception hall, each yielded for the other to enter; both faced north and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the reception hall, each yielded for the other to enter, then both faced north and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 興，主人為賓正坐西面，賓辭，主人固請，卒正坐。

translations.literal: They arose; the host urged the guest to take the primary seat facing west; the guest declined; the host pressed him persistently until he took the primary seat.
translations.idiomatic: They rose. The host urged the guest to take the seat of honor facing west; the guest declined, but the host pressed him until he finally took it.

sentences.zh: 賓還正主人坐東面亦如之。

translations.literal: The guest in turn urged the host to take the primary seat facing east, and it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The guest in turn urged the host to take the seat of honor facing east, and the same exchange followed.

sentences.zh: 賓就坐，受茶，揖，主人答揖。

translations.literal: The guest took his seat, received tea, bowed with hands joined, and the host returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: The guest took his seat, received tea, bowed with joined hands, and the host returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 飲茶敘語畢，告辭相揖。

translations.literal: When tea and conversation were finished, they took leave and bowed to each other.
translations.idiomatic: When tea and conversation were finished, they took leave and bowed to each other.

sentences.zh: 賓降階，主人送及門，復相揖。

translations.literal: The guest descended the steps; the host saw him off to the gate and they bowed to each other again.
translations.idiomatic: The guest descended the steps. The host saw him off to the gate, and they bowed to each other once more.

sentences.zh: 賓辭，主人固請，送賓大門外，視賓升輿馬，乃退。

translations.literal: The guest declined; the host pressed him persistently and saw him outside the great gate, watched until the guest mounted his carriage or horse, and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The guest demurred, but the host insisted and escorted him outside the great gate, waiting until the guest had mounted his carriage or horse before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 尚書、左都御史見大學士同。

translations.literal: When a minister or the Left Censor-in-Chief called on a Grand Secretary, it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: When a minister or the Left Censor-in-Chief called on a Grand Secretary, the protocol was the same.

sentences.zh: 賓降一品者，主人趨正賓坐，辭亦如之。

translations.literal: If the guest was one grade lower, the host hastened to the guest's primary seat; declining was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: If the guest was one grade lower, the host hastened to the guest's seat of honor, and the same exchange of polite refusal followed.

sentences.zh: 餘儀同。

translations.literal: The remaining protocol was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining protocol was the same.

sentences.zh: 二品以下京堂官翰詹科道見大學士，主人迎儀門內，送大門外，不視升輿馬。

translations.literal: When Hanlin Academy, Secretariat, and Censorate officials of the second rank and below called on a Grand Secretary, the host welcomed them inside the ceremonial gate and saw them off outside the great gate, without watching them mount carriage or horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Hanlin Academy, Secretariat, and Censorate officials of the second rank and below called on a Grand Secretary, the host welcomed them inside the ceremonial gate and saw them off outside the great gate, but did not wait to watch them mount their carriage or horse.

sentences.zh: 科道見左都御史、副都御史、尚書儀同。

translations.literal: When censorate officials called on the Left Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, or a minister, the protocol was the same.
translations.idiomatic: When censorate officials called on the Left Censor-in-Chief, a Vice Censor-in-Chief, or a minister, the protocol was the same.

sentences.zh: 五品至八品官見大學士，主人迎堂階下，賓就東階，主人導入。

translations.literal: When officials of the fifth through eighth ranks called on a Grand Secretary, the host welcomed them at the foot of the hall steps; the guest took the eastern steps and the host guided him in.
translations.idiomatic: When officials of the fifth through eighth ranks called on a Grand Secretary, the host welcomed them at the foot of the hall steps. The guest took the eastern steps and the host guided him in.

sentences.zh: 賓北面拜，辭，乃三揖，主人東面答揖。

translations.literal: The guest faced north and bowed, declined, then performed three bows with hands joined; the host, facing east, returned the bows.
translations.idiomatic: The guest faced north and bowed, demurred, then performed three bows with joined hands; the host, facing east, returned them.

sentences.zh: 賓趨正主人坐，辭，固請，卒正坐相揖。

translations.literal: The guest hastened to the host's primary seat, declined, was persistently urged, and finally took the primary seat and they bowed to each other.
translations.idiomatic: The guest hastened to the host's seat of honor, declined, was pressed to accept, and finally took the seat; then they bowed to each other.

sentences.zh: 賓西面，主人東北面坐。

translations.literal: The guest faced west; the host sat facing northeast.
translations.idiomatic: The guest faced west; the host sat facing northeast.

sentences.zh: 賓啟事畢，辭退，三揖如初。

translations.literal: When the guest had finished reporting his business and took leave, the three bows were as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the guest had finished his business and took leave, the three bows were performed as before.

sentences.zh: 主人送二門外。

translations.literal: The host saw him off outside the second gate.
translations.idiomatic: The host saw him off outside the second gate.

sentences.zh: 翰詹科道見二三品官，如賓降一等禮。

translations.literal: When Hanlin, Secretariat, and Censorate officials called on officials of the second or third rank, it followed the protocol for a guest one grade lower.
translations.idiomatic: When Hanlin, Secretariat, and Censorate officials called on officials of the second or third rank, the protocol was that for a guest one grade lower.

sentences.zh: 見四五品官，如同官禮。

translations.literal: When calling on officials of the fourth or fifth rank, it followed the protocol for officials of equal rank.
translations.idiomatic: When calling on officials of the fourth or fifth rank, it followed the protocol for officials of equal rank.

sentences.zh: 閣部寺監屬官見其長官，初見，公服詣署，升自東階，具履行陳坐案，依次向坐三揖，長官避席答揖。

translations.literal: When subordinate officials of the Grand Secretariat, ministries, directorates, and superintendent offices called on their superiors for a first meeting, wearing official dress they went to the office, ascended by the eastern steps, presented their calling cards and arranged their seat mats, bowed with hands joined three times facing each other in order, and the superior left his seat to return the bows.
translations.idiomatic: When subordinate officials of the Grand Secretariat, ministries, directorates, and superintendent offices called on their superiors for a first meeting, they went to the office in official dress, ascended by the eastern steps, presented their calling cards and arranged their seat mats, and bowed with joined hands three times facing one another in order; the superior left his seat to return the bows.

sentences.zh: 退。

translations.literal: They withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew.

sentences.zh: 若燕見，如五品官見大學士儀。

translations.literal: For informal meetings, it followed the protocol for a fifth-rank official calling on a Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: For informal meetings, the protocol was the same as for a fifth-rank official calling on a Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 國學生見國子師儀，初見，具名柬，公服詣學，自東階升堂，北面三揖，師立受。

translations.literal: Protocol for Imperial Academy students calling on their National University teachers: on a first meeting, with a calling card bearing their name and in official dress, they went to the academy, ascended the hall by the eastern steps, faced north and bowed three times with hands joined, and the teacher received standing.
translations.idiomatic: Protocol for Imperial Academy students calling on their National University teachers: on a first meeting they presented a calling card bearing their name, went to the academy in official dress, ascended the hall by the eastern steps, faced north and bowed three times with joined hands, and the teacher received the salutation standing.

sentences.zh: 侍立左旁，西面受教，畢，三揖退。

translations.literal: They stood in attendance at the left, faced west to receive instruction; when finished, they bowed three times and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They stood in attendance at the left, faced west to receive instruction, and when finished bowed three times and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 若燕見，通名，俟召乃入。

translations.literal: For informal meetings, they announced their names and entered only after being summoned.
translations.idiomatic: For informal meetings they announced their names and entered only after being summoned.

sentences.zh: 師迎階上，弟子升，揖。

translations.literal: The teacher welcomed them at the top of the steps; the student ascended and bowed with hands joined.
translations.idiomatic: The teacher welcomed them at the top of the steps; the student ascended and bowed with joined hands.

sentences.zh: 師入門，從之，北面再拜，師西面答揖。

translations.literal: The teacher entered the gate and the student followed; facing north the student bowed twice; the teacher, facing west, returned the bow with hands joined.
translations.idiomatic: The teacher entered the gate and the student followed. Facing north, the student bowed twice; the teacher, facing west, returned the bow with joined hands.

sentences.zh: 趨正師坐，師命坐，北面揖。

translations.literal: The student hastened to the teacher's primary seat; the teacher ordered him to sit; facing north he bowed with hands joined.
translations.idiomatic: The student hastened to the teacher's seat of honor. The teacher ordered him to sit, and facing north he bowed with joined hands.

sentences.zh: 師位東北面，弟子西面。

translations.literal: The teacher's seat faced northeast; the student faced west.
translations.idiomatic: The teacher's seat faced northeast; the student faced west.

sentences.zh: 茶至，揖，請問，揖。

translations.literal: When tea arrived they bowed with hands joined; when asking questions they bowed with hands joined.
translations.idiomatic: When tea arrived they bowed with joined hands; when asking questions they bowed with joined hands.

sentences.zh: 辭退，北面三揖，師皆答。

translations.literal: On taking leave, facing north they bowed three times with hands joined, and the teacher returned each bow.
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave they bowed three times with joined hands facing north, and the teacher returned each bow.

sentences.zh: 出送，師前行，弟子後隨，及二門外，弟子三揖，俟師入始退。

translations.literal: On seeing the student out, the teacher went ahead and the student followed; outside the second gate the student bowed three times with hands joined and withdrew only after the teacher had entered.
translations.idiomatic: On seeing the student out, the teacher went ahead and the student followed. Outside the second gate the student bowed three times with joined hands and withdrew only after the teacher had gone in.

sentences.zh: 翰林院庶吉士見大學士，與見教習庶吉士同。

translations.literal: When Hanlin Academy chujishi called on a Grand Secretary, it was the same as calling on their chujishi instructor.
translations.idiomatic: When Hanlin Academy chujishi called on a Grand Secretary, the protocol was the same as when calling on their chujishi instructor.

sentences.zh: 凡京朝官途遇迴避，爵秩均等，分道行，次讓道行，次勒馬俟其過，又次下馬，唯欽使即遇應迴避者，分道行可也。

translations.literal: Whenever capital officials met on the road, avoidance was required: those equal in rank and noble title traveled by separate routes; next lower in rank yielded the way; next, reined in their horses and waited for the other to pass; and lowest of all, dismounted—except that envoys bearing imperial credentials, if they met someone who ought to avoid them, might simply travel by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever capital officials met on the road, rules of avoidance applied. Those equal in noble title and rank traveled by separate routes; the next lower in rank yielded the road; the next reined in and waited for the other to pass; and the lowest dismounted—all except that an envoy bearing imperial credentials, if he met someone who ought to avoid him, need only take a separate route.

sentences.zh: 又武職民公、侯、伯以下，男以上，文職大學士以下，九卿以上，得用引馬一騎，途遇並下馬迴避雲。

translations.literal: Moreover, military nobles from civilian duke, marquis, and earl downward through baron upward, and civil officials from Grand Secretary downward through the Nine Ministers upward, were permitted one outrider; on meeting on the road, all dismounted to avoid one another—thus it was decreed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, military nobles from civilian duke, marquis, and earl downward through baron upward, and civil officials from Grand Secretary downward through the Nine Ministers upward, were permitted one outrider; when they met on the road, all were to dismount and give way to one another—thus it was decreed.

sentences.zh: 直省文武官相見禮順治間，定督、撫、學政、河漕總督，鹽政，巡視御史相見，坐次平行，餘各按品秩行禮。

translations.literal: Protocol for Meetings among Provincial Civil and Military Officials. During the Shunzhi reign it was fixed that when governors-general, governors, education intendant, Grand Canal commissioner-general, salt administration commissioner, and touring censor met, their seats were on equal footing; all others performed rites according to rank and grade.
translations.idiomatic: Protocol for Meetings among Provincial Civil and Military Officials. During the Shunzhi reign it was fixed that when governors-general, governors, education intendants, the Grand Canal commissioner-general, the salt administration commissioner, and touring censors met, their seats were on equal footing; all others performed rites according to rank and grade.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，定直省官相見，位均等者，賓至署，吏入白，啟門，自中門入，至外堂檐下降輿馬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, provincial officials' meetings were fixed: when both parties were of equal standing, when the guest reached the office a clerk entered to announce him, the gate was opened, he entered through the central gate, and dismounted from carriage or horse under the eaves of the outer hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, regulations were set for meetings among provincial officials. When both parties were of equal standing, the guest upon reaching the office was announced by a clerk, the gate was opened, he entered through the central gate, and dismounted from his carriage or horse under the eaves of the outer hall.

sentences.zh: 主人迎檐前，揖賓入。

translations.literal: The host welcomed him before the eaves and bowed with hands joined to admit the guest.
translations.idiomatic: The host welcomed him before the eaves and bowed with joined hands to admit him.

sentences.zh: 及廳事，各再拜。

translations.literal: When they reached the reception hall, each bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the reception hall, each bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 其正坐、就位、進茶、辭退，如京朝官儀。

translations.literal: Taking the primary seats, taking places, presenting tea, and taking leave followed the capital-official protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the seats of honor, taking their places, serving tea, and taking leave all followed the capital-official protocol.

sentences.zh: 屬官見長官，轅門外降輿馬，自左門入。

translations.literal: When subordinate officials called on their superiors, they dismounted from carriage or horse outside the yamen gate and entered through the left gate.
translations.idiomatic: When subordinate officials called on their superiors, they dismounted from carriage or horse outside the yamen gate and entered through the left gate.

sentences.zh: 初見具名柬，呈履行，文官司道見督撫，迎堂後屏內。

translations.literal: On a first meeting they presented a calling card bearing their name and took their place on the mat; when civil intendants called on governors-general or governors, the host welcomed them inside the screen behind the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On a first meeting they presented a calling card bearing their name and took their place on the mat. When civil intendants called on governors-general or governors, the host welcomed them inside the screen behind the hall.

sentences.zh: 及廳事，庭參則扶免，三揖，皆答揖。

translations.literal: When they reached the reception hall, if a courtyard audience was required they were assisted in exemption; they bowed three times with hands joined and each bow was returned.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the reception hall, if a courtyard audience was required they were assisted and exempted from it. They bowed three times with joined hands, and each bow was returned.

sentences.zh: 督撫正坐，司道旁坐。

translations.literal: The governor-general or governor took the primary seat; the intendant sat at the side.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general or governor took the seat of honor; the intendant sat to one side.

sentences.zh: 命坐，揖。

translations.literal: The host ordered them to sit; they bowed with hands joined.
translations.idiomatic: The host ordered them to sit, and they bowed with joined hands.

sentences.zh: 茶至，揖。

translations.literal: When tea arrived they bowed with hands joined.
translations.idiomatic: When tea arrived they bowed with joined hands.

sentences.zh: 均答如儀。

translations.literal: Each response followed the prescribed protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Each response followed the prescribed protocol.

sentences.zh: 辭出，三揖如初。

translations.literal: On taking leave and departing, the three bows were as before.
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave and departing, the three bows were performed as before.

sentences.zh: 送至屏門外，司道三揖。

translations.literal: They were seen off outside the screen gate; the intendant bowed three times with hands joined.
translations.idiomatic: They were escorted outside the screen gate, and the intendant bowed three times with joined hands.

sentences.zh: 俟督撫入，復三揖，趨出。

translations.literal: After the governor-general or governor had entered, they bowed three times again and hastened out.
translations.idiomatic: After the governor-general or governor had gone in, they bowed three times again and hurried out.

sentences.zh: 督撫次日用名柬答拜。

translations.literal: The governor-general or governor the next day returned the call with a visiting card bearing their name.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general or governor returned the call the next day with a visiting card bearing their name.

sentences.zh: 若公事謁見，常服通銜名，三揖就坐。

translations.literal: For official business calls in everyday dress, they announced their titles and names and, after three bows with hands joined, took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: For calls on official business in everyday dress, they announced their titles and names, bowed three times with joined hands, and then took their seats.

sentences.zh: 餘同前。

translations.literal: The remainder was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else was as before.

sentences.zh: 府、廳、州、縣見，庭參拜則免，府、廳揖，答揖。

translations.literal: When prefectural, sub-prefectural, department, and county officials called, courtyard audience and bowing were exempted; prefectural and sub-prefectural officials bowed with hands joined and the bow was returned.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectural, sub-prefectural, department, and county officials called, courtyard audience and full bowing were waived. Prefectural and sub-prefectural officials bowed with joined hands and the bow was returned.

sentences.zh: 州、縣揖，立受。

translations.literal: Department and county officials bowed with hands joined; the host received standing.
translations.idiomatic: Department and county officials bowed with joined hands, and the host received the salutation standing.

sentences.zh: 俱不送，不答拜。

translations.literal: In all cases there was no escort and no return bow.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases there was no escort and no return bow.

sentences.zh: 佐貳等官見，一跪三叩，不揖、不坐。

translations.literal: When deputy officials and the like called, they performed one kneeling and three kowtows; there was no bow with hands joined and no sitting.
translations.idiomatic: When deputy officials and the like called, they performed one kneeling and three kowtows; there was no bow with joined hands and no sitting.

sentences.zh: 府、廳、州、縣見司道，與司道見督撫同。

translations.literal: When prefectural, sub-prefectural, department, and county officials called on intendants, it was the same as when intendants called on governors-general or governors.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectural, sub-prefectural, department, and county officials called on intendants, the protocol was the same as when intendants called on governors-general or governors.

sentences.zh: 佐貳等官見司道，與見督撫同。

translations.literal: When deputy officials called on intendants, it was the same as when calling on governors-general or governors.
translations.idiomatic: When deputy officials called on intendants, the protocol was the same as when calling on governors-general or governors.

sentences.zh: 同知、通判見知府，柬題晚生，入自中門，用賓主禮。

translations.literal: When an assistant prefect or sub-prefect called on a prefect, the card was inscribed "Your younger junior"; he entered through the central gate and guest-host protocol was used.
translations.idiomatic: When an assistant prefect or sub-prefect called on a prefect, the calling card was inscribed "Your younger junior." He entered through the central gate and guest-host protocol was observed.

sentences.zh: 州、縣教職見督撫，儀如佐貳見司道，不迎送。

translations.literal: When department and county education officials called on governors-general or governors, the protocol was like that for deputies calling on intendants, without welcome or escort.
translations.idiomatic: When department and county education officials called on governors-general or governors, the protocol was like that for deputies calling on intendants, with no welcome or escort.

sentences.zh: 見知府，迎送屏門外。

translations.literal: When calling on a prefect, welcome and escort were outside the screen gate.
translations.idiomatic: When calling on a prefect, welcome and escort took place outside the screen gate.

sentences.zh: 見府倅，迎送堂檐下。

translations.literal: When calling on a prefectural deputy, welcome and escort were under the hall eaves.
translations.idiomatic: When calling on a prefectural deputy, welcome and escort took place under the hall eaves.

sentences.zh: 餘同。

translations.literal: The remainder was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else was the same.

sentences.zh: 見州、縣，如同、通見知府儀。

translations.literal: When calling on department or county officials, it followed the protocol for assistant prefects and sub-prefects calling on a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When calling on department or county officials, the protocol was the same as for assistant prefects and sub-prefects calling on a prefect.

sentences.zh: 司、道、府、廳見學政，入中門，禮如賓主，迎送並出堂檐。

translations.literal: When intendants, prefectural officials, and sub-prefectural officials called on the education intendant, they entered through the central gate; the rite was like guest and host; welcome and escort were both outside the hall eaves.
translations.idiomatic: When intendants, prefectural officials, and sub-prefectural officials called on the education intendant, they entered through the central gate. The rite followed guest-host protocol, and welcome and escort both took place outside the hall eaves.

sentences.zh: 學政品秩崇者，如見督撫儀。

translations.literal: If the education intendant's rank and grade were lofty, it followed the protocol for calling on a governor-general or governor.
translations.idiomatic: If the education intendant's rank and grade were high, the protocol was the same as for calling on a governor-general or governor.

sentences.zh: 州、縣見，庭參旁坐，主人答揖不答拜。

translations.literal: When department and county officials called, there was courtyard audience and side seating; the host returned the joined-hand bow but not the full bow.
translations.idiomatic: When department and county officials called, there was courtyard audience and side seating. The host returned the joined-hand bow but not the full bow.

sentences.zh: 運使見督撫、鹽院，與司道同。

translations.literal: When the transport commissioner called on governors-general, governors, or salt commissioners, the protocol was the same as for circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioners used the same meeting protocol as circuit intendants when calling on governors-general, governors, or salt commissioners.

sentences.zh: 運、判以次遞降。

translations.literal: Transport officials and assistant prefects followed in descending order of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Transport officials and assistant prefects ranked below them in turn.

sentences.zh: 武官副將以下見提督，初見具銜名、履行，披執則傳免，易公服佩刀。

translations.literal: When military officials from deputy commander downward called on a provincial commander, on first visit they presented cards bearing their titles and names and their service records; if in armor they were excused from wearing it and changed into official dress with sword.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers from deputy commander down, on first calling on a provincial commander, presented name cards with titles and service records; if they arrived in armor they were excused and changed into official dress with sword.

sentences.zh: 都司、守備不免，跪宣名，席地坐，不進茶。

translations.literal: Brigade commanders and garrison commanders were not excused; they knelt and announced their names, sat on the ground, and no tea was served.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade and garrison commanders received no exemption: they knelt to announce their names, sat on the floor, and were not offered tea.

sentences.zh: 餘儀按品遞降，與文職同。

translations.literal: The remaining ceremonies descended by rank, the same as for civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: All further ceremony followed rank in descending order, matching civil protocol.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，定直省文武官相見禮，提督見總督，入中門，至儀門下馬，升堂三揖。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, protocol for meetings among provincial civil and military officials was fixed: when a provincial commander called on a governor-general, he entered through the middle gate, dismounted at the ceremonial gate, ascended the hall, and bowed three times with joined hands.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13, provincial civil and military meeting protocol was fixed: a provincial commander entering to see a governor-general passed through the middle gate, dismounted at the ceremonial gate, ascended the hall, and bowed three times with joined hands.

sentences.zh: 總督正坐，提督僉坐，迎送不出堂檐。

translations.literal: The governor-general sat in the place of honor; the provincial commander sat beside him; reception and send-off did not extend beyond the hall eaves.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general took the seat of honor and the provincial commander sat beside him; welcome and farewell stopped at the hall eaves.

sentences.zh: 若提督兼世職者，總督西面，提督東面。

translations.literal: If the provincial commander also held a hereditary title, the governor-general sat facing west and the provincial commander facing east.
translations.idiomatic: If the provincial commander also held a hereditary title, the governor-general faced west and the provincial commander faced east.

sentences.zh: 辭出，送至堂檐下，視乘馬。

translations.literal: On taking leave, he was escorted to below the hall eaves and watched until he mounted his horse.
translations.idiomatic: On departure he was escorted to the hall eaves and watched until he mounted.

sentences.zh: 總兵見，儀門外下馬，坐則侍坐，迎、送止階上。

translations.literal: When a regional commander called, he dismounted outside the ceremonial gate; when seated he sat in attendance; reception and send-off stopped at the steps.
translations.idiomatic: A regional commander dismounted outside the ceremonial gate; he sat in attendance when seated; welcome and farewell stopped at the steps.

sentences.zh: 與巡撫見，視賓主禮唯均，以下按品差降。

translations.literal: When calling on a governor, guest-and-host protocol applied on equal terms; below that rank ceremonies descended by grade.
translations.idiomatic: When calling on a governor, host and guest met as equals; lower ranks followed descending ceremony by grade.

sentences.zh: 至滿、漢官相見，將軍、副都統與督、撫、提、鎮以敵體見。

translations.literal: As for meetings between Manchu and Han officials, generals and deputy lieutenant-generals met governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders as equals.
translations.idiomatic: In Manchu-Han meetings, generals and deputy lieutenant-generals met governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders on equal footing.

sentences.zh: 司道以下見將軍如總督，見副都統如總兵，協領、參領見督撫同司道，佐領、防禦同知府，驍騎校同州、縣。

translations.literal: Circuit intendant and below calling on a general followed protocol for calling on a governor-general; calling on a deputy lieutenant-general followed protocol for calling on a regional commander; assistant commandants and company commandants calling on governors-general or governors followed circuit intendant protocol; platoon commandants and garrison captains followed prefect protocol; cavalry captains followed prefectural or county magistrate protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendants and below used governor-general protocol when calling on a general and regional-commander protocol for a deputy lieutenant-general; assistant and company commandants followed circuit-intendant protocol with governors; platoon commandants and garrison captains followed prefect protocol; cavalry captains followed prefectural or county magistrate protocol.

sentences.zh: 不相統屬者，一以賓主禮行之。

translations.literal: Where there was no administrative subordination, guest-and-host protocol was applied throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Where no administrative tie existed, host-and-guest protocol applied throughout.

sentences.zh: 其儒學弟子員見學師，與國子生見國學師同。

translations.literal: When Confucian academy students called on their instructors, the protocol was the same as when Imperial Academy students called on their teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian academy students calling on their instructors followed the same protocol as Imperial Academy students calling on their teachers.

sentences.zh: 士庶相見禮賓及門，從者通名，主人出迎大門外，揖入。

translations.literal: Protocol for Meetings among Scholars and Commoners: When the guest reached the gate, attendants announced his name; the host came out to welcome him outside the main gate and bowed with joined hands to usher him in.
translations.idiomatic: Protocol for Meetings among Scholars and Commoners: at the gate attendants announced the guest's name; the host came out to the main gate, bowed with joined hands, and ushered him in.

sentences.zh: 及門、及階揖如初。

translations.literal: At the gate and at the steps they bowed with joined hands as before.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed again at the gate and at the steps.

sentences.zh: 登堂，各北面再拜。

translations.literal: Ascending the hall, each faced north and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall each faced north and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 興，主賓互正坐。

translations.literal: They rose, and host and guest each took the seat of honor in turn.
translations.idiomatic: They rose, and host and guest yielded the seat of honor to each other in turn.

sentences.zh: 即席，賓東主西。

translations.literal: When seated, the guest sat east and the host west.
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, the guest took the east side and the host the west.

sentences.zh: 飲茶，語畢，賓退，揖。

translations.literal: They drank tea; when conversation was finished, the guest withdrew with a bow.
translations.idiomatic: After tea and conversation, the guest bowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及階、及門，揖，辭，主人皆答揖。

translations.literal: At the steps and at the gate they bowed; on taking leave, the host returned each bow.
translations.idiomatic: At the steps and gate they bowed again; on farewell the host returned every bow.

sentences.zh: 送大門外，揖如初。

translations.literal: He escorted the guest outside the main gate and bowed as before.
translations.idiomatic: He saw the guest out to the main gate and bowed once more.

sentences.zh: 卑幼見尊長禮，及門通名，俟外次，尊長召入見，升階，北面再拜，尊長西面答揖。

translations.literal: Protocol for juniors calling on elders: at the gate the name was announced; the junior waited in the outer reception area until the elder summoned him in; ascending the steps, he faced north and bowed twice; the elder faced west and returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: When juniors called on elders: at the gate the name was announced and the junior waited outside until summoned; ascending the steps he faced north and bowed twice, and the elder facing west returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 命坐，視尊長坐次侍坐。

translations.literal: When told to sit, he sat in attendance according to the elder's seat.
translations.idiomatic: When told to sit, he took a seat beside the elder according to rank.

sentences.zh: 荼至，揖，語畢，稟辭，三揖。

translations.literal: When tea arrived, he bowed; when conversation was finished, he asked leave and bowed three times.
translations.idiomatic: When tea came he bowed; when talk was done he asked leave and bowed three times.

sentences.zh: 凡揖皆答，出不送。

translations.literal: Every bow was returned; on departure the elder did not escort him out.
translations.idiomatic: Every bow was returned, but the elder did not see him out.

sentences.zh: 若尊長來見，卑幼迎送大門外。

translations.literal: If the elder came to call, the junior welcomed and escorted him outside the main gate.
translations.idiomatic: If the elder came to call, the junior welcomed and saw him off at the main gate.

sentences.zh: 餘如前儀。

translations.literal: The rest followed the preceding protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed the protocol above.

sentences.zh: 見父執友，與見尊長儀同。

translations.literal: Calling on a father's friend followed the same protocol as calling on an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Calling on a father's friend used the same protocol as calling on an elder.

sentences.zh: 受業弟子見師長禮，初見，師未出，先入，設席正位，俟堂下。

translations.literal: Protocol for enrolled disciples calling on their teacher: on first visit, before the teacher appeared, the disciple entered first, set out the seat of honor, and waited below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Protocol for enrolled disciples calling on their teacher: on first visit, before the teacher appeared, the disciple entered first, arranged the seat of honor, and waited below the hall.

sentences.zh: 師出召見，乃奉贄入，奠贄於席，北面再拜，師立答揖。

translations.literal: When the teacher came out and summoned him in, he brought his gift of initiation, placed it on the seat, faced north and bowed twice, and the teacher stood and returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the teacher came out and summoned him, he brought his initiation gift, set it on the seat, faced north and bowed twice, and the teacher stood and returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 興，謹問起居。

translations.literal: He rose and respectfully inquired after the teacher's health.
translations.idiomatic: He rose and respectfully asked after the teacher's health.

sentences.zh: 命坐乃侍坐。

translations.literal: When told to sit, he sat in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Only when told to sit did he take a seat in attendance.

sentences.zh: 有問，起而對。

translations.literal: When questioned, he rose to reply.
translations.idiomatic: When asked a question, he rose to answer.

sentences.zh: 辭出，三揖，不送。

translations.literal: On taking leave he bowed three times; the teacher did not escort him out.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving he bowed three times; the teacher did not see him out.

sentences.zh: 常見侍坐，請業則起，請益則起。

translations.literal: On regular visits he sat in attendance; when requesting instruction he rose; when requesting further clarification he rose.
translations.idiomatic: On regular visits he sat in attendance; he rose both to request instruction and to ask for further clarification.

sentences.zh: 師有教，立聽。

translations.literal: When the teacher gave instruction, he stood and listened.
translations.idiomatic: When the teacher spoke, he stood and listened.

sentences.zh: 命坐乃坐。

translations.literal: Only when told to sit did he sit.
translations.idiomatic: He sat only when told to do so.

sentences.zh: 師問更對，仍起而對。

translations.literal: If the teacher questioned him again, he still rose to reply.
translations.idiomatic: If the teacher questioned him again, he still rose to answer.

sentences.zh: 朝入暮出均一揖。

translations.literal: Entering in the morning and leaving in the evening, each time he bowed once.
translations.idiomatic: Whether entering in the morning or leaving in the evening, he bowed once each time.

sentences.zh: 與同學弟子，以齒序之。

translations.literal: With fellow disciples, precedence was ordered by age.
translations.idiomatic: Among fellow disciples, precedence went by age.
